mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong parent investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A (Hague Apostille): notarized certified copy followed by apostille issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B (non-Apostille state): notarization followed by authentication of the local ministry of foreign affairs and consular legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate. Paths are mutually exclusive and never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Current Status Certificate) of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: certified copy plus Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B: certified copy plus local faith-affairs authentication plus PRC consular legalization. No sequential use of apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney resolving WFOE incorporation and appointing the PRC legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: notarization by a Hong Kong Notary Public followed by Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B for non-Apostille states: notarization plus local competent-authority authentication plus PRC consular legalization. Use only one path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Hong Kong investor company (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: certified true copy from the Companies Registry plus Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B: certified true copy plus local authentication plus PRC consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming account relationship and satisfactory banking conduct for the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank in Hong Kong
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: bank officer signature notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public followed by Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B: bank officer signature notarized and then submitted for PRC consular legalization after local authentication. Do not apply both paths to the same letter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and current UBO register of the Hong Kong investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Secretary of the Hong Kong investor company under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: notarized company secretary certificate plus Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Parallel Path B: notarized company secretary certificate plus local authentication plus PRC consular legalization. Never combine apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be completed against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and all PBOC and PRC domestic sanctions and AML/CFT watchlists. The WFOE must identify each direct and indirect shareholder, all beneficial owners at or above the 25-percent threshold, all directors and legal representatives, senior management, and authorized signatories. The compliance team must run enhanced PEP status checks through commercial and government databases, verify the source of funds for inbound capital contributions, document negative news and politically exposed person hits, and retain screening evidence for not less than five years. Investors from high-risk third jurisdictions require additional enhanced due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration Online Application Platform / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must be in simplified Mandarin Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier statutory composition: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry descriptive phrase, and organizational form, for example Shanghai + trade name + Low-Code Software + Co., Ltd. The trade name may not consist solely of pinyin or English letters unless expressly approved. The English company name is auxiliary only and does not replace the Chinese registered name. Foreign investor names must be transliterated in a phonetically and culturally acceptable manner, and the industry phrase must match the approved business scope, including ISIC 6201 visual web template and no-code software services. Any use of prefectural, provincial, national, or cross-border terms requires special examination.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall obtain the written rejection notice and file a written administrative reconsideration application with the immediately higher SAMR authority within 60 days, or initiate administrative litigation within six months under the PRC Administrative Litigation Law. The appeal must restate the proposed Chinese name, cite the specific supporting legal grounds, attach the prior rejection notice, include evidence of trademark and public-record clearance, and request reconsideration by the name review committee. An alternative backup name must be reserved in parallel to prevent delay to the WFOE incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not acceptable in Mainland China. PRC market-entry registration rules, municipal tax bureaus, and commercial banks require a physical, verifiable business address in the registered city for VAT registration, corporate bank account opening, and invoice control-system enrollment. For the ISIC 6201 no-code website builder industry, a leased office, incubator space, or a government-approved clustered address in a free trade zone may be accepted only if the WFOE can demonstrate actual management presence, business continuity, and operational substance. The tax authority will reject an address if it appears to be a mere mail-forwarding desk with no staff, no records, and no management control, and commercial banks will refuse to open settlement accounts at such an address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 35-45 percent probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by municipal SAMR or tax authorities within the first 12 months after WFOE formation. Inspection checklist: original lease contract and rental payment vouchers; corporate seal and statutory books; employment contracts and social insurance records; office signage and active computer equipment; VAT invoice system records and bank statements; availability of the legal representative or authorized management; and physical presence of staff relevant to the declared low-code software business. Failure to satisfy any item materially increases the risk of administrative deregistration, blacklisting for VAT invoicing, and forced change of the registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 7, 8, 23, 24, 26, 37, 46, 47, 49, 51, 52, 56, 57, 62, 63 and 64; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746); Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (2021 Edition); PRC Foreign Investment Law (2020).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (e.g., Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation), Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Desk.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form, Articles of Association, and Foreign Investment Information Report submitted through the SAMR one-stop online enterprise registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a WFOE in ISIC 6201 computer programming services. The registered capital is fixed in the Articles of Association and may be fully subscribed without immediate cash payment; however, Article 47 of the PRC Company Law requires each shareholder to pay all subscribed capital within five years after the date of issuance of the business license, except for restricted industries. There is no blocked or escrow account mandated by company law; the sole foreign shareholder must, as a matter of foreign exchange regulation, open a capital contribution account on the FDI information system, register with SAFE through the designated bank, and remit capital in a freely convertible currency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD. (Limited Liability) (the 'Company'), adopted by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, pursuant to Article 46 of the PRC Company Law and Article 12 of the Articles of Association, on this ____ day of ______, 20____, at the Company's registered office.

WHEREAS the Company has been incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the laws of the People's Republic of China; and

WHEREAS the incorporators have appointed the undersigned as the first directors to serve until the first shareholders' meeting; and

WHEREAS the Board considers it necessary and desirable to organize the statutory, financial, and operational affairs of the Company.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. Share Capital Subscription and Payment. The Board confirms the registered capital of the Company as stated in the approved Articles, namely [RMB ______], divided into [_______] ordinary shares of equal par value. Such capital shall be fully subscribed by the sole shareholder [HK Parent Company] and paid up in accordance with Article 47 of the PRC Company Law within five years from the date of the business license. The Board authorizes the General Manager to open a foreign-exchange capital contribution account with a SAFE-designated bank, to receive the paid-in capital remittance, to file the Foreign Investment Information Report, and to make all filings with the local Market Supervision Administration and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

2. Banking Authorization and Signing Mandate. The Board designates [______________ Bank, ________ Branch] as the Company's principal banking partner. Any two of the Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer are authorized to sign banking mandates; one signatory shall always be the General Manager or Chairperson. The authorized signatories may open accounts in RMB and foreign currencies, execute wire transfers, purchase instruments, and establish online banking credentials, subject to the Board's internally approved delegation of authority.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board accepts [registered address in PRC] as the Company's registered office. The General Manager shall file the lease agreement, landlord title certificate, payment voucher, and landlord identity copy with the local Market Supervision Administration within ten working days of business license issuance. Statutory books, seals, and Articles shall be kept at that address.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [Name] as General Manager/President, [Name] as Chairperson and legal representative, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as Company Secretary. The legal representative shall represent the Company in all external filings; the Supervisor shall supervise Board conduct, financial statements, and statutory compliance; the Company Secretary shall maintain registers and proceed with regulatory filings.

5. Common Seal and External Advisors. The Board approves the carving and dual-control custody of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. The Board appoints [Law Firm] as legal counsel and [Accounting Firm] as statutory auditor.

6. This resolution shall take effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts. This resolution supersedes all prior oral arrangements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Entity Structure Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) - One-Stop Online Enterprise Registration Service Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor's formation agent must access the provincial enterprise registration portal operated by the local Market Supervision Administration and complete the online name reservation module. The applicant must identify the legal form as a limited liability company, specify the investment source as Hong Kong SAR, and list three prioritized trade names in the prescribed format. The name examiner verifies against prohibited terms, similar or identical registered names, and negative-list constraints. Upon approval, the system generates a Name Reservation Notice valid for six months, which allows the applicant to proceed to the establishment application.
required_dossiers: Online Name Reservation Application
Notarized and apostilled/legalized Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong parent company
Certificate of Good Standing of the Hong Kong parent company
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Passport or identity card copy of the proposed legal representative
Passport or identity card copy of the proposed supervisor
Brief description of the proposed business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited elements, the examiner will give a written rejection with reason; the applicant may resubmit with a revised distinctive element within five working days or seek administrative reconsideration from the same authority within fifteen working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Articles to SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR), Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Name Reservation Notice, the formation agent must draft the Chinese version of the Articles of Association reflecting the registered capital subscribed, the one-shareholder structure, and ISIC 6201 business scope. All corporate documents issued by the Hong Kong parent must be translated into Chinese and notarized or legalized under the applicable convention. The application, including the Foreign Investment Information Report, is signed by the legal representative and submitted electronically. The SAMR registration officer reviews the capital rules and business scope for conformity with the Negative List; if the dossier is complete, the authority issues the business license and the unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Notice
Articles of Association signed by sole shareholder
Board resolution of Hong Kong parent approving the WFOE establishment
Certificate of incorporation and Good Standing of parent (legalized)
Proof of registered office: lease agreement, landlord title certificate, landlord identity
Identity documents of legal representative, directors, supervisor and general manager
Foreign Investment Information Report
Power of attorney to the local formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR suspends the application, the applicant may cure the deficiency within thirty days by submitting the missing documents or amending the Articles; the suspension notice will cite the exact legal issue. In case of an administrative denial, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the same Market Supervision Administration within sixty days or bring suit in the competent People's Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business License and Carving of Company Seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) licensed seal engraving company and SAMR service counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After substantive approval, the SAMR prints the Unified Social Credit Code business license and delivers it electronically or by counter collection. The applicant must immediately proceed to a Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving enterprise, carrying the original business license and legal representative identification. The engraver produces the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal, and records the impressions in the PSB seal filing system. The legal representative or a written agent must sign a seal handover register, after which each seal is held under separate custody. No contract or bank account may be opened without the sealed business license.
required_dossiers: Original Unified Social Credit Code business license
Name Reservation Notice
Legal representative original identity document
Seal engraving application form endorsed by SAMR
PSB seal recordation form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the PSB seal system rejects the recordation because of a suspected irregularity, the applicant must resubmit the missing owner identification or updated license. If rejection continues, the applicant may apply to the local PSB Administrative Service Center for formal review, and a further denial can be appealed as an administrative action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social, Foreign Exchange and Bank Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local office; Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a designated bank; People's Bank of China (PBOC) account administration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first calendar month, the WFOE must complete electronic tax registration with the local office of the State Taxation Administration, verify taxpayer status, set up accounting records, and apply for invoice quota. The entity must also complete social insurance registration with the Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for all employees. In parallel, the sole shareholder must work with a SAFE-designated bank to register the FDI information, open a capital settlement account, and receive the paid-in capital. The company then opens a basic deposit account at a commercial bank under PBOC account administration rules and submits all anti-money-laundering KYC files. All licenses and account documents are filed in the corporate data room.
required_dossiers: Business license original and seal impressions
Articles and first board resolution approving banking signatories
Legal representative and second signatory identity documents
Tax registration application form
Social insurance registration form
FDI foreign exchange registration form, capital source proof, and parent board resolution
Lease agreement and utility bill for registered office
AML/KYC questionnaire, beneficial ownership statement, and expected transaction turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority fails to issue a tax registration, the applicant may resubmit corrected taxpayer information through the portal or attend the tax service hall for manual processing. If the bank declines the account for AML/KYC reasons, the company may provide enhanced due diligence letters from the parent bank and audited parent financial statements. Arbitrary rejections may be escalated to the bank branch compliance officer or reported to the local PBOC, and administrative appeals to the provincial tax bureau are available within thirty days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the registered business scope covers visual web template and low-code web application development under ISIC 6201, which involves no physical manufacturing, petrochemical processing, heavy assembly, or warehouse operations. No industrial licensing board authorization is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - the entity is classified as a pure digital services provider; the only registration is the SAMR business license. For mainland-China-based SaaS delivery, an additional ICP filing or value-added telecommunications license may be separately triggered if the product is hosted for PRC users, but that is not a physical operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE), as delegated to the local Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA filing or full EIA report is required because the project is not listed in the Categorized Management List of Construction Projects for Environmental Impact Assessment (2019 Edition) and involves no land development, construction, or pollutant generation. Only standard commercial-office environmental performance obligations apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater, zero regulated air emissions, zero hazardous waste. The company must comply with municipal waste classification rules, including disposal of e-waste and office paper through licensed municipal channels, and any air-conditioning or HVAC systems within the leased office must meet the applicable indoor air quality hygienic standards if fresh-air systems are installed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to a pure digital service; however, the leased office premises must have a valid fire safety inspection or archival record issued by the local Fire and Rescue Department pursuant to the Fire Protection Law. The company must designate a workplace safety officer, maintain portable fire extinguishers, post evacuation plans, and provide annual fire-fighting training. Structural load approval is not required unless the company installs on-site server racks or battery backup units; in such case, the landlord must confirm floor bearing capacity in writing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online portal is the nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) e-filing platform integrated with the official STA website.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in mainland China, the entity first obtains a business license from the Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Within 30 days of incorporation, the WFOE completes tax registration at the competent State Taxation Administration branch; the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) shown on the business license is accepted as the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for both corporate income tax and VAT purposes. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China may be required to obtain a tax identification number through its withholding agent or by direct registration with the STA for treaty relief and China-sourced income declarations; however, the WFOE itself is a Chinese resident enterprise and therefore holds a full 18-digit TIN from inception.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law does not provide check-the-box elections or pass-through classification for limited liability entities; a WFOE is taxed as a resident enterprise at entity level. No elective hybrid mismatch treatment is available in the PRC tax framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All business entities must complete tax registration upon incorporation regardless of turnover. For VAT classification, annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 trigger mandatory registration as a General VAT Taxpayer; entities with annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000 are classified as Small-Scale Taxpayers with simplified levy rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates under the Golden Tax Phase IV digital governance framework. VAT invoices, including Special VAT Invoices and Fully Digitized Electronic Invoices, must be issued through the STA's authorized electronic invoice service platform. Invoicing data is transmitted in real time to the tax authority, with system-generated unique invoice numbers and digital stamps for anti-fraud integrity. Enterprise accounting systems must interface with the national e-invoice platform using authorized APIs and authentication mechanisms; no unaudited standalone invoice issuance is permitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported physical goods are eligible for the 0% VAT rate and corresponding input VAT refund or rebate under the PRC export tax rebate regime. Qualifying cross-border services, including eligible information technology services such as software platform access and low-code website builder services supplied to overseas recipients, may also be zero-rated or exempt when the service recipient is outside China, the service is rendered and consumed wholly outside China, and the WFOE satisfies the statutory documentation and record-keeping requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (Export Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or logistics transport document evidencing export movement
Commercial Invoice and Export Sales Contract
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-currency collection receipt proving repatriation of export proceeds
Export Tax Rebate Declaration and underlying input VAT invoice records supporting the refund claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities cross-check customs export data, VAT invoice issuance, and foreign exchange collection records through the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Any zero-rating claim that cannot be substantiated is retrospectively clawed back, with the VAT refund reversed and late payment interest charged. Under the Law on Tax Administration and Tax Collection, penalties may range from 50% to 500% of the underpaid or improperly refunded tax depending on the degree of falsity. Where fraudulent export rebate documentation is established, criminal liability may attach to the enterprise and responsible officers, including monetary penalties and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC); for the Hong Kong SAR mirror, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China's FX regime is governed by SAFE under a managed floating exchange rate system. Current account foreign exchange receipts and payments, including software service export fees, software subscriptions, and profit remittances, are generally eligible for conversion upon presentation of authentic supporting documents; no advance SAFE approval is required for current account transactions, but banks perform thorough documentary verification. Capital account flows, by contrast, are subject to a registration-based licensing system: inbound FDI must be reported under the Foreign Investment Information Report and SAFE FDI registration, the capital contribution must be lodged in a designated capital account, and subsequent RMB conversion for operating purposes must respect the negative list and the restricted use of capital account funds. Those funds cannot be applied to securities investment, entrusted loans, or repayment of domestic RMB loans outside the permitted scope. Dividend repatriation is treated as a current account profit remittance and requires audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, a board resolution and bank verification; the WFOE must have fully settled its corporate income tax and completed the annual SAFE reporting. In summary, convertibility is full for current items and controlled but progressively liberalised for capital items.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since the 2012 SAFE reform, mainland China has no mandatory export proceeds surrender ratio; the WFOE may keep 100% of its foreign currency receipts in a foreign currency settlement account or may convert them into RMB at its election. The statutory compliance requirement is that export/service proceeds be repatriated into a domestic bank account within the normal settlement period, generally no later than 90 days after the underlying customs declaration for goods or the invoice/contract due date for services; accounts receivable outstanding beyond this window must be reported to SAFE through the bank and may require documentary justification. For service exports such as no-code SaaS subscriptions, the bank verifies the contract, invoice, settlement voucher and platform payout report in place of customs documents. The effective mandatory conversion ratio is therefore 0% to 100% voluntary conversion, with no forced surrender to the central bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account) and Basic Operational Currency Account
RMB Basic Deposit Account with integrated SAFE foreign exchange settlement and cross-border RMB window

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and General Operational RMB Account
Capital Verification Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs, including Airwallex, Currenxie, Payoneer, and Hong Kong-licensed quasi-banks, have no lawful authority to provide onshore mainland corporate accounts to a PRC WFOE. Under the Law on Commercial Banks of the PRC and PBOC administrative licensing rules, deposit-taking and corporate account services in mainland China may be performed only by licensed banks or bank-type financial institutions approved by the regulatory authorities. EMIs are therefore viable only as offshore collection/payment channels for the Hong Kong parent, not for the WFOE's domestic or FDI treasury operations. The WFOE's inbound capital injection must land in a mainland bank account that is registered with SAFE; any EMI interception would break the FDI registration and create a regulatory violation. For software subscription revenue collected through Stripe and Paddle, settlement can be arranged through licensed payment institutions with cross-border payment licenses or through a Hong Kong corporate account, but the WFOE should not attempt to repatriate proceeds through unlicensed EMI rails because PBOC payment network settlement and SAFE monitoring would be compromised. Overall feasibility rating: Low as primary treasury rail; permissible only for auxiliary offshore cash management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under prevailing PBOC and bank KYC policy, corporate account opening for a WFOE requires in-person verification of the legal representative or a duly authorised representative at a physical bank branch in mainland China. The majority of tier-1 banks will mandate at least one in-person interview with the statutory legal representative and the financial controller; a purely remote or consular proxy procedure is not generally permitted. Some banks permit a notarised power of attorney in favour of an onshore manager if the foreign legal representative cannot travel, but the bank will still require the authorised manager to appear with original corporate chops, business licence, articles of association, and the legal representative's notarised and apostilled ID documents. Remote video verification may supplement, but cannot replace, the physical interview for foreign-funded entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore intermediate ownership structure - HK/BVI holding layers above the mainland WFOE with no clear natural-person UBO visible on the commercial registry extract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized corporate registry search from the Hong Kong Companies Registry and all offshore incorporators, certificate of incumbency from the registered agent, chronological share register and all transfers since incorporation, trust or foundation deed where applicable, certified passport copies of each individual holding more than 25% through the chain, signed UBO declaration in the bank's standard template, group organisational chart, and source-of-wealth statement for the capital being contributed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value digital subscription collections routed through Stripe and Paddle, creating perceived risk of unidentifiable third-party money movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Paddle payout and settlement statements for at least six months, standard terms of service and SaaS subscription agreement, merchant identification program output showing customer name, email, IP and transaction ID, refund and dispute register, chargeback history, PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance, and a business model narrative explaining expected average transaction size and velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential disguised cross-border profit shifting or mis-priced intra-group service fees between the HK parent and mainland WFOE, particularly for development fees or IP royalties paid to Hong Kong.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intra-group service agreement with scope, rates and calculation basis, arm's length transfer pricing documentation prepared under China's State Administration of Taxation Bulletin 2017 No. 6, evidence of actual service delivery such as DevOps tickets, product release logs, employee timesheets and electronic communications, tax filing and payment receipts for withholding tax, and SAFE-approved outbound payment verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geographic restrictions concern because the no-code website builder platform is globally accessible, raising exposure to customers in OFAC, EU, or UN sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered acceptable-use policy and territorial restrictions, geolocation and IP screening logs, automated sanctions screening report for the prior quarter, customer onboarding verification showing government-issued identification for business customers, policy on account closure for sanctioned users, and a compliance officer attestation confirming no sanctioned counterparty was knowingly serviced.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound FDI equity investment from the HK parent to the mainland WFOE must be routed via an international wire in the investing entity's name to the WFOE's dedicated foreign exchange capital account at a tier-1 onboarding bank. The bank must be the same institution handling SAFE FDI registration through the Foreign Exchange Administration System. The SWIFT field 70 must quote 'FDI Equity Injection under the relevant SAFE registration number', with the purpose code consistent with direct investment and the investor name matching Hong Kong Companies Registry records. After credit, the bank verifies that the source is the HK parent's own account and not a third-party nominee, applies the negative-list business scope check, converts the proceeds to RMB or retains foreign currency, and issues a capital receipt notification. A licensed Chinese CPA then performs capital verification and issues the capital verification report required for market regulator filings. The WFOE must submit the report to the Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System and complete SAFE's annual FDI reporting. No portion of the capital may be used for purchasing unrelated real estate, securities investment, entrusted loans, or repayment of domestic RMB loans unless expressly exempted under SAFE pilot policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements should be processed on SWIFT MT103 for ordinary operating payments such as international software tooling subscriptions, cloud hosting bills, and third-party professional fees, accompanied by the underlying contract and invoice. For significant equipment or physical licensing imports from Hong Kong, a commercial letter of credit can be issued through the WFOE's issuing bank to the Hong Kong beneficiary; the LC terms must match import customs and regulatory declarations where goods are involved. Documentary collections are acceptable for low-risk periodic disbursements where the seller is known and the documents, including bills of lading, invoices, and packing lists, are simple; however, for software-only transactions, MT103 with full contract data is more efficient and avoids processing delays. All outward payment items require the bank to obtain the correct SAFE purpose code, such as trade, service fee, or royalty; inaccurate purpose codes are a leading cause of rejection. RMB outward remittances should be routed through CIPS-compatible banks, while non-RMB transactions are settled over standard SWIFT.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla FX forwards (USD/CNY, HKD/CNY, EUR/CNY) for up to 12 months, provided the underlying exposure is verified by contract, invoice, or audited profit remittance plan; executed with a SAFE-covered bank and booked without speculative intent.

FX swaps are permitted for temporary conversion of surplus foreign exchange into RMB and back, matched to a real business cash-flow need, with corresponding SAFE registration and bank FXD contract records.

Cross-currency swaps are allowed only for documented long-term foreign currency debt or capital expenditure; the notional, interest, and principal flows must be consistent with the underlying loan agreement and require SAFE reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted in the onshore China market; the Hong Kong parent may hedge CNH/USD exposure using CNH deliverable forwards or CNH NDFs in Hong Kong, but such instruments must not be booked in the mainland WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) for a Hong Kong private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration fees escalate by interval: HK$1,680 (USD 215.38) within 3 months; HK$3,360 (USD 430.77) within 6 months; HK$5,040 (USD 646.15) within 9 months; HK$6,720 (USD 861.54) beyond 9 months; continued default is a continuing offence exposing the company and each responsible officer to fines and daily default fines, and the company may be administratively struck off by the Companies Registry under section 745 of the Companies Ordinance after Gazette notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate annual renewal (Business Registration Ordinance registration renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Office), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date printed on the current certificate, being normally one year after commencement of business; renewal should be made within the month before the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts an additional HK$300 (USD 38.46) penalty; unregistered or unrenewed operation is a criminal offence under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) with fines up to HK$5,000; continued non-renewal may lead to the business being treated as not in operation and, together with other defaults, a ground for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) for corporations, with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Taxpayer Records Office), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the tax return, subject to automatic extension or granted extension by the Inland Revenue Department; typical annual issue dates depend on the accounting period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by due date attracts late filing penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) that escalate with continued default; unpaid estimated or provisional profits tax may be assessed by the Inland Revenue Department, and persistent non-compliance may lead to prosecution and jeopardize the company's good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A together with individual employee remuneration particulars from Form BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Employer's Return), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of the Employer's Return; normally around early April for remuneration paid in the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or incorrect filing is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; penalties up to HK$10,000 and potential additional penalties up to treble the amount of tax undercharged; continuing default may lead to prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Directors' approval and circulation of financial statements (and auditor's report where applicable) for the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company members (no filing with a government registry for private companies unless requested by the Revenue Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and approved by the board no later than six months after the end of the financial year; a private company must circulate or send the statements to members in accordance with its articles and sections 380-381 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), generally within the same six-month approval window or such shorter period as the articles require
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding HK$300,000 and a daily default fine not exceeding HK$7,000 for non-compliance with reporting obligations under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance; no administrative strike-off occurs solely for this default, but persistent non-compliance affects overall standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Hong Kong incorporated company must appoint one or more certified public accountants (practising) as auditor for each financial year unless it validly obtains an exemption under section 359D of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). A private company is exempt from statutory audit only if it is not a listed company, bank, insurer, securities dealer, licensed leveraged foreign exchange trader, or non-profit or other excluded company and it qualifies as a small private company or a member of a small private company group. A small private company must satisfy at least two of the following three quantitative conditions for the relevant financial year: (i) total annual revenue not exceeding HK$100,000,000 (approximately USD 12,820,513); (ii) total assets not exceeding HK$100,000,000 (approximately USD 12,820,513); and (iii) number of employees not exceeding 100. The exemption is available only after the passing of a resolution by the members and the delivery of a directors' solvency statement, and it does not remove the legal need to prepare true and fair financial statements unless the company is dormant. Any company failing the exemption conditions is subject to compulsory independent CPA audit, with no lower threshold applying to banks, insurance companies, licensed corporations, and large private companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities or the SME Financial Reporting Framework and Standard issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), with the profits tax computation overlay required by the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual public UBO confirmation filing. Instead, every company must maintain a Register of Significant Controllers under Part 17A of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) at its registered office; the register must identify individuals with significant control (25% or more of shares or voting rights, control of the board, or right to influence the company), and any change in a significant controller's information must be recorded within 7 days. The register must be made available to law-enforcement officers on demand, without an annual filing. Share allotments must be reported to the Companies Registry by Return of Allotment (Form NS1) within 30 days after allotment; share transfers require immediate updating of the Register of Members and are subject to Hong Kong stamp duty on the instrument of transfer (generally 0.2% of consideration), but they are not filed at the Companies Registry. The Annual Return (NAR1) annually confirms the statement of capital, shareholders, directors, and secretary and thereby captures the relevant corporate-control status as at the return date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Chief Executives
Minute Book of general meetings and directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per annum for registered office address, corporate secretarial filing support, and compliance calendar administration; the range varies with service provider, number of jurisdictions, and director or secretary arrangements.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 per annum for a low-risk small-to-medium Hong Kong private company in the software or no-code website builder business, excluding any group audit consolidation work; fees increase if the company exceeds the small company audit exemption or requires consolidated financial statements in Hong Kong.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) certification; 20% reduced rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with taxable income up to RMB 3 million (effective 5% for income up to RMB 1 million and 10% up to RMB 3 million for 2023-2027); super deduction of 200% for eligible R&D expenses; 15% rate for encouraged industries in Western China; no statutory patent box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, A-class) submitted electronically via the State Taxation Administration electronic filing system (e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau); related schedules include Form A200000 for quarterly prepayments and Form G100000 for annual related-party transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 5 months after the end of each fiscal year (by May 31); quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 days after each quarter end; non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties is declared and paid at the time of payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all business activities, including SaaS subscription fees, website design services, licensing of the no-code builder software, and any ancillary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all global revenue in full, including payments received via Stripe/Paddle from foreign customers. For sales routed through the Hong Kong parent or other related parties, ensure the transfer price is at arm's length and supported by a contemporaneous TP study. Do not offset intercompany costs against revenue; report cross-border royalties or service fees separately for withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including direct cloud hosting, developer salaries, third-party software licenses, and depreciation of technology equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany fees or charges from the Hong Kong parent (e.g., management fees, shared IT costs) are deductible only if supported by valid contracts, actual provision of services, and arm's length pricing; otherwise, add them back as non-deductible. If any payment constitutes a royalty or interest to a non-resident, it must be separately subjected to withholding tax; failure to withhold makes the expense non-deductible and triggers penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit (book profit) after deducting all expenses from gross income, as reflected in PRC GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the accounting profit with the tax return; any prior-year adjustments or accounting errors must be declared. A WFOE that constantly reports near-zero or negative profit while paying high service fees to the Hong Kong parent will attract TP scrutiny and may be adjusted to reflect arm's length profit allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments: increase for non-deductible expenditures, TP adjustments, entertainment expense disallowance, and related-party interest limits; decrease for tax-exempt income and deductible non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has related-party transactions with the Hong Kong parent, attach Form G100000 and adjust profit to conform with the arm's length standard. Even without a formal TP audit, self-initiated adjustments are strongly recommended for related-party financing (thin capitalization limits under EIT Law Article 46), service fees, and IP royalty payments. Withholding tax on outbound interest/royalties is not an income tax deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting carried-forward losses, tax-exempt income, and allowable deductions; the tax base on which the 25% CIT is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general five-year loss carryforward applies; ten years is allowed for high-tech enterprises and SME technology firms. Losses of the Hong Kong parent or other group entities cannot be offset against Chinese taxable income. Any further TP adjustment will increase taxable income and may eliminate a loss carryforward, triggering immediate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT calculated at the applicable rate (25% or preferential rate) after applying tax credits, including foreign tax credits and tax concessions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the correct rate; do not treat Chinese dividend withholding tax as part of income tax. The WFOE is a Chinese resident; foreign tax credits are irrelevant for profits earned in China. If the Hong Kong parent charges interest or royalties, those payments are not included in taxable income but are subject to separate WHT, which must be reported and paid at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax paid during the year through quarterly prepayments and the final balance payable or refund due after the annual settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance by May 31; any late payment incurs a daily surcharge. Separately, when declaring dividends to the Hong Kong shareholder, the WFOE must withhold the applicable withholding tax (5% with valid DTA treatment, otherwise 10%) and remit it to the tax authority at the time the dividend is declared. This Box does not capture that withholding; it is reported on the non-resident withholding return (Form F-311).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return: RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases; RMB 10,000 for serious cases (Article 62, Tax Administration Law). Late payment: daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax (Article 32). Understating taxable income or TP non-compliance: penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax (Article 63); criminal liability arises if the underpayment exceeds RMB 100,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable, leading to imprisonment up to 7 years (Article 201, Criminal Law). Failure to withhold on non-resident payments: penalty of 50%-300% of the unrecovered tax (Article 69); company directors and responsible officers may face personal liability and travel bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (reduced to 5% under the China-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement for a Hong Kong resident company that is the beneficial owner and directly holds no less than 25% of the WFOE's capital)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% preferential dividend withholding rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, complete the 'Non-resident Taxpayer Entitlement to Treaty Benefits' application form, and submit it (along with the China-HK DTA beneficial ownership self-declaration, audited financial statements, shareholding diagram, and evidence of economic substance in Hong Kong) to the Chinese competent tax authority before the dividend distribution. The WFOE may withhold at the 5% rate only after the tax authority issues a notice of treaty entitlement; otherwise, the statutory 10% must be withheld and the Hong Kong shareholder may claim a refund through an amended application. Substantial compliance requires the Hong Kong entity to have real business operations (employees, office, and decision-making in Hong Kong) to satisfy the Principal Purpose Test under the 2019 Protocol.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% withholding on gross amount paid to non-residents; under the China-HK DTA, 5% for standard intellectual property (copyrights, patents, trademarks, software) and 7% for industrial/commercial/scientific equipment royalties. Interest: statutory 10%; under the DTA, 7% if the beneficial owner is a bank or financial institution, otherwise 10%. The reduced treaty rates require submission of a TRC and beneficial ownership declaration before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory if the WFOE has related-party transactions exceeding any of the following in a year: RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; or RMB 100 million for other related-party transactions (including services). Master File is required if the WFOE is part of an MNE group with consolidated annual revenue exceeding RMB 5.5 billion and the WFOE's related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million. Country-by-Country Report is required if the group's consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China's General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Article 47) and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures apply a substance-over-form standard; the Chinese WFOE must demonstrate substantive commercial activity (employees, business decision-making, and risk-bearing capacity) in mainland China to sustain its residency and to justify the conclusion of intercompany contracts. For the Hong Kong parent to enjoy DTA benefits, it must satisfy Hong Kong's Economic Substance Regime (Inland Revenue Ordinance amendments) by performing Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Hong Kong—including equity investment management, IP licensing, and corporate treasury functions—in a manner proportionate to the income it derives. Without such substance, China can apply the Principal Purpose Test and deny treaty relief, reclassifying the arrangement as abusive.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Failure to File Related-Party Transaction Report
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately under-reports taxable income by paying excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to its Hong Kong parent or other related parties, and omits the required Annual Related-Party Transaction Report (Form G100000) from its CIT filing to conceal the TP scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41 and 44 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law; Public Notice [2016] No. 42 of the State Taxation Administration. The tax authority may adjust the taxable income under the arm's length standard, impose a TP interest premium of up to 5 percentage points above the base rate (Article 121, Tax Administration Law), and apply a penalty of 50%-500% of the additional tax assessed (Article 63). The adjustment can be retroactive for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false return are personally and jointly liable for the tax deficiency if they directed the transfer of assets out of the company; tax authorities may freeze personal bank accounts, impose travel bans and exit restrictions (blacklisting), and initiate criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion, leading to imprisonment up to 7 years and confiscation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a conduit or shell entity with no office, employees, or decision-making substance in Hong Kong, yet the WFOE applies the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate under the China-HK DTA without substantive proof of beneficial ownership, causing tax revenue loss in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Principal Purpose Test (PPT) inserted by the 2019 Protocol denies treaty benefits; the State Taxation Administration will reassess the dividend at the 10% statutory withholding rate, collect the 5% shortfall plus 0.05% daily surcharge, and impose a penalty under Article 63 (50%-500% of the unpaid tax). Article 69 of the Tax Administration Law also penalizes the WFOE as the withholding agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE who knowingly participated in the shell structure are jointly liable for the unpaid withholding, subject to civil asset restitution, travel bans, and personal forfeiture. Criminal liability under Article 203 of the Criminal Law (falsifying tax returns) can result in imprisonment up to 5 years and heavy fines for responsible persons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Cross-Border Royalty and Interest Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE makes substantial interest payments to the Hong Kong parent on intercompany loans and pays software royalties for the no-code builder engine, but deliberately fails to withhold the statutory or treaty WHT on these outbound payments, and also claims these expenses as CIT deductions on its annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 37, 38, and 69 of the Tax Administration Law; the WFOE is the statutory withholding agent and is subject to a penalty of 50%-300% of the unwithheld tax. The interest and royalty payments are disallowed as tax deductions if WHT is not paid, resulting in additional CIT at 25%. Criminal sanctions apply where the amount withheld but not remitted exceeds RMB 50,000, leading to prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and the finance director are personally liable under the Company Law for failing to perform withholding obligations; the tax authority may apply to the court for personal assets to be seized, impose exit bans, and institute criminal prosecution. In severe cases, directors face imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine equal to the tax lost.
